title: Principles of statistical modeling 
---

What is Statistical Modeling?

Statistical modeling is the process of creating a representation of a real-world process using mathematics/statistics. Modeling involves identifying the underlying patterns and relationships within data to construct theoretically motivated models that can explain observations, make predictions, or test hypotheses.

Statistical modeling comprises:

- Variables: The measurable characteristics or attributes that can vary among subjects or observations or over time.
- Parameters: The constants in the model that quantify the relationship between variables.
- Assumptions: The conditions under which the model operates, such as the distribution of errors or the independence of observations.

Statistical modelling comprise a wide range of approximations that include but it is not limited to: 

- Linear Regression Models: Describe the linear relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.
- Generalized Linear Models (GLMs): Extend linear models to accommodate non-normal response distributions.
- Time Series Models: Analyze data points collected over time.
- Machine Learning Models: Utilize algorithms to train systems and make predictions.
